CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the ongoing management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on reviewing treatment efficacy and addressing new symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to his current treatment regimen. While he continues to benefit from improved sleep patterns, he notes a resurgence of anxiety symptoms, particularly during work-related stressors. Mr. Smith states he has maintained an average of 7 hours of sleep per night, but has recently experienced increased nocturnal awakenings, leading to feelings of fatigue during the day.
He reports that his tension-type headaches have recurred slightly, now presenting at a frequency of 2-3 times per week, with an intensity of 3-4 out of 10. The patient has been using ibuprofen 400 mg as needed but expresses concern about the increased reliance on medication for headache relief. He attributes some of the recent anxiety and headache episodes to heightened project deadlines and personal stressors.
Mr. Smith has continued his bi-weekly acupuncture sessions and practices mindfulness exercises; however, he feels that these strategies are becoming less effective in the face of current stress. He has also begun incorporating yoga into his routine, which he finds somewhat beneficial in managing his anxiety.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (increased usage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work effectively as a software engineer, although current project demands have increased his stress levels. He remains active in his running group and has recently started attending yoga classes, which he hopes will assist with anxiety management. His dietary habits remain healthy, with continued abstinence from alcohol and minimal caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Increased anxiety levels noted; sleep quality has slightly declined; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has increased; intensity moderate; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues; no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears fatigued but engaged. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with some distress noted.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Due to increased anxiety symptoms, consider increasing sertraline to 250 mg daily. Lorazepam usage may be increased to 1 mg twice weekly as needed for acute anxiety episodes. Continue to encourage regular CBT attendance and mindfulness practices. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Assess for any sleep hygiene issues and reinforce the importance of a consistent sleep schedule. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Maintain amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily. Given the increased headache frequency, consider a follow-up in one month to reassess and determine if a medication adjustment is warranted. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to persist with physical activity, yoga, and mindfulness practices. If fatigue does not improve, consider referral to a sleep specialist for further evaluation.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-12-01 to monitor symptoms, evaluate the effectiveness of medication adjustments, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
